accused_occupation: Senior police officer (on deputation as Director (Vigilance & Security), BBMB)
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance: the accused was founder/president of the tennis association (HLTA) in which the victim was an enrolled member, and he called her to his office
statutory_provisions: IPC s.354 (outraging modesty of a woman); FIR also cited s.509; s.306 addition was set aside
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PW-13), corroborated by other witnesses; documentary (Memorandum); handwriting expert opinion (disputed); enquiry statements
aggravating_circumstances: Accused was a very senior police officer; victim was an unmarried minor girl (about 15)
mitigating_circumstances: Old age; health ailments; responsibility for unmarried daughter with congenital heart disease; past meritorious service; prolonged trial
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.354 IPC; sentenced to 6 months RI and fine of Rs. 1,000
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision dismissed (01.09.2010); Sessions court had enhanced sentence to 1.5 years RI on 25.05.2010
offence_finally_established: IPC s.354 (outraging modesty of a woman)
neutral_facts: The victim, a 15-year-old girl, was an enrolled member of a lawn tennis association whose office was in a garage of a house owned by the accused, who was the association's president and a senior police officer. The accused had told the victim's father that he would arrange special coaching for her at the association, and he asked that she come to his office. On the day in question, the victim and a companion went to the office at the accused's request. The accused asked the companion to fetch the coach, and she left the room. On returning, the companion saw the accused holding one of the victim's hands while his other arm was around her waist and he was pulling her towards his chest to embrace her, while the victim tried to push him back with her free hand. On seeing the companion, the accused released the victim and sat down. The companion later found the victim crying and the victim described what had happened. The two girls initially decided not to tell their parents, fearing the accused's position. On a later date the victim disclosed the incident to her parents, and a memorandum describing the incident, signed by the victim and others, was submitted to state authorities. A state official conducted an enquiry and recorded statements. The victim's signature on the memorandum was disputed, and a handwriting expert was examined; several witnesses testified that they saw the victim sign it. The victim's father testified that the accused had visited him on an earlier day, asked that the victim not be sent abroad, and asked that she come to his office; the companion's account was consistent with this. The ball picker and the coach were not examined. A formal FIR was later registered and the investigation was carried out by the CBI, which filed a charge-sheet.
physical_harm: No injury described; forcible holding and embracing of the victim while she tried to push the accused away
premeditation_planning: Not found as premeditation; the court inferred the requisite culpable intention (knowledge/intent to outrage modesty) from the sequence of events
motive: alleged: intent to molest the victim, per the victim's account; the defence alleged rivalry between tennis associations, which the court found unsupported
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-13 on the molestation; PW-15's account of the accused's earlier visit and summons, corroborating PW-13; statements of PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4 and PW-15; the Memorandum and witness identification of the victim's signature
witness_credibility: PW-13 found reliable, consistent and corroborated; withstood cross-examination; no reason to depose falsely; the court also found the other witnesses independent and not shown to be inimical
post_offence_conduct: Per the complainants' account, the accused had left for Chandigarh when they went to his office on 14.08.1990; not a court finding
bail_history: Bail allowed by the Supreme Court by order dated 11.11.2010 on special leave petition; no other bail history stated
trial_duration: offence: 12.08.1990; trial judgment: 21.12.2009; High Court: 01.09.2010; Supreme Court: 23.09.2016
legal_representation: Appellant: K.V. Viswanathan, Sr. Adv., with Ms. Priyanjali Singh, Dhananjay Ray and Mehul M. Gupta (Advs.). Respondents: Ms. Vibha Datta Makhija, Sr. Adv. (for CBI), with Rajiv Nanda, Ajay Sharma and others; Vikas Mehta for respondent no. 2
investigation_status: FIR No. 516 of 1999 registered at PS Panchkula under ss.354 and 509 IPC; investigation by CBI; CBI charge-sheet dated 16.11.2000 under s.354 IPC
procedural_irregularity: Delay in registering a case: the enquiry report recommending a case (1990) was not acted upon by the State government, and the FIR was registered only in 1999 after High Court and Supreme Court orders. Court found the 6-day delay in complaining to the SHO explained
appeal_history: Trial court (21.12.2009): convicted s.354, 6 months RI and Rs. 1,000 fine. Sessions (25.05.2010): accused's appeal dismissed; CBI and complainant's enhancement appeals allowed, sentence raised to 1.5 years RI. High Court (01.09.2010): revision dismissed. Supreme Court (23.09.2016): conviction upheld, sentence reduced to period undergone
prosecution_argument: Occurrence proved by PW-13's unimpeachable eyewitness testimony, corroborated by PW-15 and others; signatures on Memorandum proved by witnesses present, handwriting expert evidence weak; Memorandum not manipulated; non-examination of ball picker and coach draws no adverse inference; enquiry officer competent and his statements admissible under s.157; rivalry irrelevant
defence_argument: Act impossible in a garage office with people present; prosecution story false and framed by complainant side and senior officers; victim's signature forged; 'Sathi Khiladi' planted; no police complaint lodged; enquiry without jurisdiction; IAS lobby rivalry; ball picker and coach not examined; witness improvements and discrepancies
legal_principle_applied: Essential ingredients of s.354 IPC (woman assaulted; criminal force used; force used intending to outrage modesty); intention/knowledge may be inferred from circumstances; a single truthful, consistent eyewitness suffices; uncorroborated handwriting expert evidence is weak; adverse inference only where evidence is withheld; delay explained by social context
precedent_relied_upon: Vidyadharan v. State of Kerala (2004) 1 SCC 215; Tarkeshwar Sahu v. State of Bihar (2006) 8 SCC 560; Mobarik Ali Ahmed v. State of Bombay AIR 1957 SC 857; Smt. Bhagwan Kaur v. Shri Maharaj Krishan Sharma (1973) 4 SCC 46
sentencing_rationale: Given the accused's old age, physical condition and health ailments, the court held it not expedient to send him back to jail and reduced the sentence to the period already undergone as a special case
judicial_mitigating_factors: Old age and physical condition of the accused, with the other factors cited (health ailments, daughter's illness, past service, prolonged trial)
